papers_read.title_as_printed: A transformer-based multi-features fusion model for prediction of conversion in mild cognitive impairment (Zheng et al., Methods 204 (2022) 241-248)
Class activation attention transfer neural networks for MCI conversion prediction (Luo et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 156 (2023) 106700)

what_each_reports.P-82: Transformer fusion on FreeSurfer DKT cortical features (5 measures x 62 regions) from baseline T1 MRI, 249 ADNI MCI (104 sMCI/145 pMCI, 3-year conversion; MCI-to-CN reverters counted as sMCI). One random split 200/25/24: test accuracy 83.3% (20/24), AUC 0.888, sensitivity 0.727, specificity 0.923. No confidence interval; 10-fold CV reported only in Supplementary Table S2 (not in the extract).
what_each_reports.P-3: 3D CNN ensemble with class-activation attention transfer on whole baseline T1 MRI volumes, ADNI1/2, 298 sMCI/295 pMCI (36-month conversion), Wen et al. benchmark splits, 5-fold CV: accuracy 74.61% (variance 0.002, i.e. SD about 4.5 points across folds), AUC 0.780, sensitivity/specificity 0.75/0.75. The authors note that tuning and selecting on the same 5-fold CV may bias the estimate upward.

quantity_a: sMCI vs pMCI (3-year) accuracy from 310 FreeSurfer ROI features of baseline T1 MRI, ADNI subset of 249 (58% pMCI, reverters in sMCI), single 24-subject test set
quantity_b: sMCI vs pMCI (36-month) accuracy from whole-volume baseline T1 MRI, ADNI1/2 subset of 593 (50% pMCI), 5-fold CV
incompatible_if_same: No. Even treating them as the same quantity, 83.3% on 24 test subjects (binomial 95% interval roughly 64-93%, computed here) contains 74.61%, and P-3's fold-to-fold SD of about 4.5 points does not exclude 83%. P-82 claims to beat earlier MRI deep-learning models 'from 73.95% to 78.79%', but P-3 makes no claim about P-82's method, so no ordering is refuted.

gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (different, partly overlapping MCI subsets)
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal, no external cohort
gates.modality_family: match at family level (structural MRI), but the input representation differs: tabular FreeSurfer ROI measures vs voxel-level whole-brain images

endpoint_and_metric: compatible in type (accuracy, 3-year conversion) with differences in label definition (P-82 counts reverters as sMCI) and class balance (58% vs 50% pMCI), which move accuracy without any change in discrimination
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 83.3% and 74.61% are below 0.97. P-82's test set of 24 makes its point estimate imprecise.
independence: Both use ADNI; MCI cohorts likely overlap in part. Different groups (Lanzhou/Cardiff; La Trobe/Monash), no shared authors.
grounds: The two accuracies are statistically compatible: P-82's 83.3% rests on 20 of 24 test subjects, an estimate that cannot exclude P-3's 74.61%, and neither paper reports uncertainty that excludes the other.
Two different methods each report a score on their own ADNI subset, and neither study claims an ordering the other refutes, which the rule reads as not incompatible.

The quantities also differ (FreeSurfer tabular features vs image-level input; reverters counted as sMCI and 58% pMCI in P-82 against 50% in P-3), which is why the 2026-09-19 human reading recorded documented incommensurability; under the ordered outcome list, compatibility is decided first.

evidence_quotes.quote: we split our 249 subjects randomly into three groups, including the training dataset (n = 200), the validation dataset (n = 25), and the testing dataset (n = 24).
The proposed model achieved 83.3% accuracy and an AUC of 0.888 (Fig. 2), with a sensitivity of 0.727 and a specificity of 0.923
Finally, we extracted multiple cortical measurements including volume (VOL), cortical thickness (CT), curvature index (CD), folding index (FD), and surface area (SA) for 62 brain regions

the classification performance of the proposed model also outperformed previously developed deep learning models for classifying pMCI versus sMCI based on MRI data [22,53-55], which ranged from 73.95% to 78.79%.
A limitation of our experimental setup is the use of 5 fold cross validation for both tuning and selecting the models. This may lead to an optimistically biased evaluation of the model performance.

record_defects: resolution_note 'Genuine architectural conflict ... gap 8.7%' treats a point-estimate gap as a conflict; the 24-subject test set in P-82 cannot support it.

interpretation 'Pre-computed anatomical ROIs (FreeSurfer) beat end-to-end voxel learning (CNN) on small datasets' is not a claim either paper tests; neither compares the two input types on a shared split.
genuine=true and genuine_conflict=true remain in the record alongside resolution_status documented_incommensurability and status rejected; the flags contradict the status.
The bridging list (C-index and other-task papers) is not apt for this pair.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Toward documented_incommensurability rather than false_positive: an adjudicator who weighs the input-representation and label-definition differences before compatibility. Toward a real disagreement: P-82's supplementary 10-fold CV showing an accuracy whose interval excludes P-3's on a comparable label definition, which would still leave the representation difference.
